Title: August 13 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Study Session
Overview: The council convened a special meeting and held an executive session to receive confidential legal advice on potential new litigation, approved unanimously. In the study session, staff previewed the 2027 through 2030 citywide strategic plan process and gathered council feedback, then presented goals for the Civic Area East Bookend development partnership RFP and asked for feedback before release. The council also gave staff non-binding direction to draft resolutions opposing several state ballot measures and supporting the county early childhood measure, the graduated income tax, and two others, with formal votes to follow at a later meeting.

Topic1.Title: Special Meeting and Executive Session on Potential Litigation
Topic1.Summary: The council convened a special meeting and voted unanimously to enter executive session under Colorado law and the city charter to receive confidential legal advice on potential new litigation. Participants were listed for the record and no concerns about improper discussion were raised. The special meeting was then reconvened and closed at 6:01 p.m.

Topic2.Title: Strategic Plan 2027 to 2030 Check-In
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the process for developing the next four-year citywide strategic plan, including a world of possibilities document with about 41 inputs drawn from roughly 170 staff proposals. The presentation described a prioritization rubric, the relationship to the comprehensive plan and budget tiers, and a timeline with a community workshop on November 14 and a January pre-retreat study session. Council members raised concerns about council ownership of the process, access to budget versus actuals and prior plan outcomes, and the need for a clearer prioritization methodology. Members suggested adding items such as a Title 9 rewrite, a two-year budget process, and a category for services no longer core to the city's mission.

Topic3.Title: Civic Area East Bookend Development Partnership RFP
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented the goals and process for a public-private development partnership on the city-owned East Bookend of the Civic Area, with an optional West Bookend, to deliver a year-round food destination with the Boulder County Farmers Market, arts and culture uses, and park connections. The RFI drew nine responses that broadly supported the partnership model, and the RFP is planned for late summer with a partner selected in early 2027. Council discussed selection committee membership, ground-floor commercial uses, developer experience, park safety and activation, ongoing park maintenance costs, phasing, and the Arboretum Path, which is currently outside the funded phase. Council members asked staff to make the community vision goals more explicit and to consider affordability, economic synergy with downtown, and total cost of ownership.

Topic4.Title: 2026 State and County Ballot Measure Positions
Topic4.Summary: Staff explained that the city can take an official position on ballot measures only through a council-adopted resolution and asked whether council wanted drafts for any measures. The county early childhood care mill levy and several state measures were reviewed, including initiatives on fentanyl penalties, law enforcement reporting, sports participation, minors' surgeries, road funding, natural gas rights, and the graduated income tax. Council members gave straw-poll direction to draft non-binding resolutions opposing the fentanyl measure and the road funding measure, supporting the county child care measure, the graduated income tax, and Proposition NN, and supporting the sporting goods tax revenue for conservation measure only after further review. Formal votes on the resolutions are expected at a later regular meeting.
